name: Store Finder
description: Browse a directory of store locations and find the ones nearest to you
backend_requirements: Access control: anyone may browse stores; require auth for creating, updating and deleting stores; admin endpoints are restricted to the admin account
Stores: any signed-in user may create, update and delete any store; DELETE /api/stores/:id removes the store permanently

Store validation: name is a required non-empty string of at most 100 characters, address a required non-empty string of at most 255 characters, phone an optional string of at most 30 characters; latitude is a required number from -90 to 90 and longitude a required number from -180 to 180
GET /api/stores lists active stores sorted by name; ?query= matches name or address case-insensitively

Proximity search: when GET /api/stores gets both ?lat= and ?lng=, it keeps only stores within ?radius= kilometres (default 25, at most 500) of that point, sorts them nearest first and sets each store's distance_km to the great-circle distance rounded to one decimal; without a location distance_km is null; lat without lng (or the reverse) or an out-of-range value answers 400
On first start with an empty store table, seed 8 sample stores spread across a few cities so the finder is usable straight away
Deactivated stores (is_active false) are left out of GET /api/stores and answer 404 on GET /api/stores/:id; the admin overview still lists them
Errors answer with a JSON object {"detail": "<message>"}: 400 for invalid input, 401 without a valid token, 403 for a non-admin on admin endpoints, 404 for unknown ids
frontend_requirements: Everyone sees the store list and store details read-only; signed-in users also get the add, edit and delete controls, and visitors see a 'Sign in to manage stores' prompt in their place
Sign-in and registration forms that call /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register; keep the token for later requests, show the signed-in username and offer sign-out
Store list: name, address and phone of each store, with a search box that filters by name or address

A 'Use my location' button asks the browser for the visitor's position, then lists the nearby stores with their distance in km and a radius selector; if permission is denied the plain list stays and a short note explains why
A simple location plot that places each listed store (and the visitor, when known) by latitude and longitude, drawn by the page itself without external map tiles
Clicking a store opens its details: name, address, phone and coordinates, with a button that copies the coordinates
Add and edit store forms that show the API's validation messages next to the form; delete asks for confirmation first
admin_requirements: Admin overview: every store, active or not, with total, active and inactive counts
Toggle a store's active status from the overview

api_endpoints.description: List active stores, by name or nearest first when a location is given

query.query: Case-insensitive text matched against name and address
query.lat: Latitude of the search point (-90 to 90); requires lng
query.lng: Longitude of the search point (-180 to 180); requires lat
query.radius: Search radius in kilometres when lat and lng are given (default 25, at most 500)

api_endpoints.description: Replace a store's fields (name, address, latitude and longitude required; an omitted phone is cleared)

data_models.name: Store
data_models.description: A store location; distance_km is computed per request and not stored

fields.name: string (required, max 100 chars)
fields.is_active: boolean (default true; false hides the store from public endpoints)

admin_api_endpoints.description: Admin overview: every store with counts
